tasks.title: Orchestrator: rebase retry baselines over committed external changes
tasks.objective: Stop retries from treating already-committed, out-of-scope changes made by other work as the task's own (the PLAN-001, PLAN-002 and PLAN-003 write-scope workarounds). The first attempt records base_commit; a retry baseline overlays the current content of files that are outside write_globs, not on a protected-path denylist, present and byte-identical to HEAD, and changed only by commits in base_commit..HEAD that touch no write_globs file. Each overlaid file is recorded in base.json and shown in prepare output and in the implementer and reviewer packets. Every Git error, non-ancestor base, merge commit or missing base fails closed; only a repository without .git behaves as before. In-scope changes, uncommitted changes, scope checks and all gates are unchanged.

acceptance.AC1: The first prepare records base_commit (HEAD) and whether the tree was dirty; a retry fails closed if base_commit is missing, not an ancestor of HEAD, or the range holds a merge commit or a Git error, and a legacy attempt without base_commit needs an explicit --base-commit that is an ancestor of HEAD and whose tracked files match the recorded base hashes
acceptance.AC2: Only files outside write_globs and outside a denylist (orchestration/gates.json, tools/, tests/test_orchestration.py, orchestration/prompts/, .github/, AGENTS.md, docs/CONTRACTS.md), present in HEAD with working-tree bytes equal to HEAD, and changed solely by commits touching no write_globs file are folded into base[files]; orchestration/tasks.json is eligible only if the retrying task's own entry is unchanged; at most 50 files; each is recorded in base.json as {path, sha256, commits}
acceptance.AC3: Disposable-repository tests cover: mixed in/out-of-scope commit not rebased; implementer out-of-scope commit rebased and audited (documented residual risk); tainted-then-reverted file; amend/rebase/reset makes the base a non-ancestor; merge commit; revert to base content; rename and delete; dirty, assume-unchanged and skip-worktree files; denylisted paths; own tasks.json entry changed; Git error, missing git and no .git; the 50-file cap; legacy base.json with and without --base-commit; and the abuse tests are shown to fail against the pre-change tool
acceptance.AC4: The rebased paths and commits are printed by prepare and listed in implementer.md and reviewer.md; the rule, its denylist and residual risks are documented; the existing orchestration tests pass unmodified and base[files] plus source-before keep their meaning

A two-parent merge contributes the files from git diff-tree -m --first-parent --no-commit-id --name-only -r -z --no-renames and taints them if it touches a write_globs file; root commits, merges with more than two parents and any Git error still fail closed. tools/ stays denied unless the owner passes --allow-new-tool <path> for that exact path and the path passes the name and base checks. acceptance.AC1: Merges: a retry over a two-parent merge succeeds and records the merge hash in commits for each file in its first-parent diff; tests cover a merge that touches a write_globs file only through the first-parent diff (taints), the main-merged-into-feature and feature-merged-into-main directions (the latter taints conservatively and is documented), a merge that reverts an out-of-scope file to base content (no overlay), and a tainted file later reverted by a merge (stays tainted). A merge with more than two parents, a root commit brought in by unrelated history, a non-ancestor base and each enumerated Git failure (unresolvable base, rev-list, rev-parse --parents, diff-tree, show) fail closed
acceptance.AC2: tools/: without --allow-new-tool nothing under tools/ is overlaid. With it, only the named path, only a direct child tools/<name>.py, regular file mode (no symlink or gitlink), absent from both the base_commit tree and the original base inventory (compared with casefold and NFC normalisation), whose stem is not in sys.stdlib_module_names, not an importable installed top-level module, not sitecustomize, usercustomize, conftest, __init__ or __main__, and whose casefolded name is not a gate file (orchestrate.py, check_tests.py). The flag is recorded in base.json with each overlaid path's size and first three lines; every other denylist entry, the 50-file cap and the byte-equal-to-HEAD condition are unchanged
acceptance.AC3: Disposable-repository tests cover every AC1 and AC2 case plus a stdlib-named file, a package directory, a .pth file, a case-variant of a gate file, a symlinked and a gitlink tools/ entry, and that orchestration/gates.json, tests/test_orchestration.py and the other denylist entries stay denied even when absent at base; the abuse tests are shown to fail against the pre-change tool, and a mutation that disables each new guard is caught by at least one test
acceptance.AC4: At a stated HEAD, a small read-only call to Workflow.rebase_candidates with attempt-01 of AERIS-012's base.json and --allow-new-tool tools/audit_publication.py reports no refusal and lists tools/audit_publication.py in the audit list; the command and its output are stored as an artifact; prepare is not called
acceptance.AC5: The ADR quotes the old and new rules side by side and lists residual risks; EVALUATION_LOOP.md documents the merge rule, the flag and the AERIS-012 command; all other orchestration tests and gates pass unmodified

tasks.title: QUT multi-sequence evaluation harness
tasks.objective: Measure detection, track continuity, off-target and false-alarm proxies and forecast error on all 15 pinned QUT sequences with the PLAN-011 pre-registered measures and development/holdout split, so detector and tracker changes are compared on labelled real video instead of one unlabelled clip.

acceptance.AC1: A manifest pins every QUT sequence video (published LFS SHA-256), target-label CSV, one or more other-aircraft CSVs and target-info.csv (published Git blob SHA-1 plus measured SHA-256) at the AERIS-031 revision with sizes, dates, global-frame bounds and the PLAN-011 split; the runner refuses unpinned or mismatched files, never fetches other release files, checks dev/holdout overlap and records it, and media stays Git-ignored
acceptance.AC2: The runner composes the accepted tracker (selectable config file, AERIS-027 low-score pass) and forecasters with a selectable detector profile on video only, opens labels after runtime outputs are fixed, and reports per-sequence and pooled PLAN-011 measures 1-9 with supports and availability reasons, plus profile, detector config and weight hashes, tracker config hash, code commit and frame resolution; it refuses variants missing from the candidate list, stamps results with the list SHA-256, stride and timestamp source, compares two reports on the common forecast subset and evaluates the PLAN-011 selection rule
acceptance.AC3: Holdout runs require a written selection record; the optional dev-only synthetic pan shifts frames and labels by the same seeded offset; unit tests cover label and other-aircraft loading, bounds, association, every measure, pooling, the selection rule including zero baselines, split enforcement and the pan offset on small synthetic inputs; the unchanged baseline is recorded on the development split for the fast profile (selection baseline) and fast-zoom (secondary), with limitations and unavailable metrics stated

tasks.title: Tracker-guided full-resolution crop
tasks.objective: Raise recall on small aircraft by running the detector, each frame, on native-resolution model-sized crops around confirmed or lost tracks' causally propagated positions, feeding those detections to the tracker as extend-only measurements, in batch, live and evaluation paths; switchable, off by default in live, and selected under the PLAN-011 rule.
